_comment: Language instruction templates for atomic actions (subtasks).
The action names are the ones passed to `Base_Task.start_subtask` / `Base_Task.subtask`.
Templates of a task can be overridden by adding `description/subtask_instruction/<task_name>.json`;
an action missing from the task file falls back to the templates below.
Placeholders are filled from the `info` dict of the subtask. `{a}`, `{b}`, ... are arm tags
and are rendered as 'the left arm' / 'the right arm', every other placeholder is rendered as
'the <value>' (or the object description of `objects_description/<value>.json` when it exists),
so templates must NOT write the article themselves.
A template whose placeholders are not all provided by the subtask is skipped.

pick.schema: {A} is the object being picked up, {a} is the arm that picks it up
seen: Reach for {A} and grasp it with {a}.

place.schema: {A} is the object being placed, {B} is the target it is placed on, {a} is the arm that places it

move.schema: {A} is the object being moved, {B} is the destination, {a} is the arm that moves it

lift.schema: {A} is the object being lifted, {a} is the arm that lifts it
seen: Pick {A} up into the air with {a}.

push.schema: {A} is the object being pushed, {a} is the arm that pushes it

pull.schema: {A} is the object being pulled, {a} is the arm that pulls it

open.schema: {A} is the object being opened, {a} is the arm that opens it

close.schema: {A} is the object being closed, {a} is the arm that closes it

press.schema: {A} is the object being pressed, {a} is the arm that presses it

handover.schema: {A} is the object being handed over, {a} is the arm giving it, {b} is the arm receiving it

back_to_origin.schema: {a} is the arm returning to its rest pose
seen: Move {a} back to its home position.
Bring {a} back to the rest pose.
